title: Networking tools
subtitle: Reachability, path, DNS, sockets, whois, and packets

cards.meaning: Test the network — they do not replace persistent config
cards.notes: ping=alive? traceroute=hops? host/dig/nslookup=DNS. netstat=listening? whois=owner? tcpdump=wire?

cards.meaning: Send ICMP echo requests; replies mean reachable (unless ICMP blocked)
cards.notes: Runs until Ctrl-C. No reply ≠ always down — firewalls often drop ping.

cards.meaning: Stop after N packets
Show hop-by-hop path toward a host (each router that answers)
cards.notes: Map of the road, not just destination alive.

cards.meaning: Similar hop-by-hop path idea; often no root needed
Short DNS lookup: name → address
Reverse lookup: address → name
DNS lookup with full answer (question, answer, extra)
Reverse DNS lookup (PTR)
Query DNS (interactive or one-shot); shows your resolver and the answer
cards.notes: Shows which DNS you asked (#53) and whether the answer is authoritative.

cards.meaning: Your resolver (often from /etc/resolv.conf), port 53
DNS
cards.notes: Also appears as a listening port for dnsmasq in netstat examples.

cards.meaning: Cached/recursive answer, not from the domain’s own SOA servers
Reverse lookup; IP octets reversed under in-addr.arpa
cards.notes: One IP can have several names.

cards.meaning: Reverse DNS namespace; IP octets are reversed under it
Display connections, routing tables, interface stats, and more
All TCP sockets, numeric (no reverse DNS)
Server waiting for connections
Session is up
Listening TCP only, with PID/program name
cards.notes: -l listening, -p process. Root needed to see other users’ processes.

cards.meaning: CUPS (printing)
Service listens locally only — not reachable from other hosts
Look up NIC/registrar records (owner, contacts, dates) — not a DNS A lookup
cards.notes: Answers “who owns this domain?”, not “what IP is it?”

cards.meaning: Print packets on an interface that match an expression
Capture on that interface
Traffic to or from that IP (source or dest)
Match TCP/UDP port 80; write raw pcap to a file
cards.notes: -w writes raw pcap, not text (open later in Wireshark).

cards.meaning: Filter with src/dst and AND/OR; quotes keep and/or for tcpdump, not the shell
cards.notes: 3389 = RDP, 22 = SSH. Parentheses for AND/OR grouping.
